title: Nearest Village Finder: Closest Village
description: Find the nearest village to any point with the Nearest Village Finder — name, distance and compass direction from open map records. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a point deep in farmland resolves to a village two miles northeast that the driver had never heard of — rural geography's everyday magic, and deliveries' everyday need.
quick_answer: The Nearest Village Finder scans OpenStreetMap's village records around a point and reports the nearest village with its distance and compass direction. Search a place or use your location, press find, and read the answer — built for rural addresses and deliveries where 'near X' needs a name.
steps_intro: Out where the towns run out, the village is the address. Find yours:

body.t: “Nearest village?” is the question rural directions actually run on. The finder answers with distance and direction — the
A listing's 'rural setting' becomes a measured village distance — the shop, the pub, the school run's real anchor.
Tell the recovery service the nearest village and direction and you have given them a map reference a human can use.
Villages mean water, food and buses. Route planning through village country starts with knowing where they are.
Name plus distance plus compass direction is a complete rural reference: 'two miles northeast' orients a human; coordinates orient a machine. The finder gives the human version.
The map's settlement classification decides — village between hamlet and town in the record's terms. Local pride may grade settlements differently; the data's word is the one reported.

faq: Straight-line distance from your point across OpenStreetMap's village records, reported with the compass direction to it. Roads may wind further; the crow's measure is the ranking's honest basis.
Does it work outside the US and Europe?
Wherever OpenStreetMap carries settlement records — most of the inhabited world, at varying depth. Sparse-data regions return sparser answers, labelled by their scarcity.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — search a place name or enter a point instead.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Village names and classifications vary by source and language; the record's version is shown as recorded.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
It returned a hamlet, not a village.
In sparse records the nearest settlement of village class can be far; where the finder widens the net, it reports what it actually found, class included.
Bilingual regions record both; the finder shows the record's name forms. Both are right — maps carry communities' names, not verdicts.
